title: WORLD.build still seeds a CPU torch.Generator and draws with it into modules already moved to `device` -- the exact device-mismatch crash b95c4a4 fixed in FAB.build, LM.build_model and SIG.build, left unrepaired in the fourth copy of the same pattern.
failure: Any run with the default levers (WORLD_ENABLED defaults to True -- src/world/levers.py:182 `enabled = Lever(True, ...)`) and RUN_DEVICE=cuda. world.api.build() does `gen = torch.Generator(device="cpu")` (line 112), then builds `w.encoder`, `w.world_proj`, `w.qproj` and moves each `.to(device)` (lines 117-119), then at line 136-140 draws IN PLACE into those already-moved parameters with `t.uniform_(-0.1, 0.1, generator=gen)`. torch requires an in-place random op's generator and its tensor to share a device; a cpu generator writing into a cuda tensor raises RuntimeError before the world model exists -- on every RUN_DEVICE=cuda run, the same failure b95c4a4's own commit message names as 'EVERY GPU RUN WOULD HAVE CRASHED... A device mismatch that only fails on the hardware you cannot test on is the worst shape this defect takes.' WORLD.build is not a stub (no NotImplementedError; it is called from spine/compose.py:1947 as `sysm.world = world_api.build(...)`) and was already written (commit 2088e3d, before round 1's findings were even recorded), so this is not new or incomplete code -- it is the one instance of the pattern the repair missed. Verified: `grep -rn 'torch.Generator(device=' src/*/api.py` shows fabric/api.py:189, lm/api.py:314 and sig/api.py:121 all now read `torch.Generator(device=device)` (the fixed form) while world/api.py:112 is the lone remaining `torch.Generator(device="cpu")`. Also verified WORLD.build runs and returns a live World on RUN_DEVICE=cpu (the crash is latent there, exactly as FAB/LM/SIG were before their fix), so nothing in the CPU-only suite this project runs would catch it.
evidence: src/world/api.py:112 `gen = torch.Generator(device="cpu")`; :117-119 `w.encoder = nn.Sequential(...).to(device)`, `w.world_proj = nn.Linear(...).to(device)`, `w.qproj = nn.Linear(...).to(device)`; :136-140 `for t in list(w.encoder.parameters()) + list(w.world_proj.parameters()) + list(w.qproj.parameters()): if t.dim() >= 2: t.uniform_(-0.1, 0.1, generator=gen)`. Compare src/fabric/api.py:189, src/lm/api.py:314, src/sig/api.py:121, all `torch.Generator(device=device)` post-repair, and b95c4a4's own commit message: 'FAB.build, LM.build_model and SIG.build each seeded a torch.Generator(device="cpu") and then drew with it into parameters already moved to the target device... All three now create the generator on the target device and allocate modules there directly' -- WORLD is not named among the three and its copy of the identical code shape was not touched by that commit (git log -- src/world/api.py shows build() last modified in 2088e3d, before b95c4a4).
fix: Change line 112 to `gen = torch.Generator(device=device)`, matching the repair already applied to FAB.build, LM.build_model and SIG.build. Also normalize line 145-147 (`k = torch.empty(nmax, route_d)` drawn on an implicit-cpu tensor, then `w.keys.copy_(k.to(device))`) to draw directly into `w.keys` in place with the device generator, for the same reason the other three packages stopped using the intermediate-cpu-tensor-then-copy shape.

title: The resume/replay branch of build_vocabulary still measures bytes_per_token on a dropout-free segmentation, even though b95c4a4 fixed this exact defect on the build path -- the repair is only half-applied.
failure: CKPT_RESUME set to a real snapshot with TOK_DROPOUT>0 (a resumed continual-learning run, the case this project's numbers are measured across). build_vocabulary's replay branch at line 253 calls `_segment(vocab, sample, dropout=0.0, stream=None)` unconditionally, ignoring `tok.dropout` and the just-minted `vocab.dropout_rng`, so `vocab.bytes_per_token` on every resume is measured on the deterministic (no-dropout) segmentation -- the exact P1-H16-shaped error the same commit fixed three lines away on the fresh-build path (line 312: `_segment(vocab, sample, dropout=float(tok.dropout), stream=stream)`). Reproduced end to end: built a vocabulary with TOK_DROPOUT=0.3 (bytes_per_token=1.8785, measured with dropout, correct), wrote it out in the `entries` format _replay_merges reads, then resumed by pointing CKPT_RESUME at that file with TOK_DROPOUT=0.3 again. The resumed Vocabulary reports bytes_per_token=2.25 (the dropout-free number) against 1.8801 for a segmentation of the identical text actually drawn with dropout=0.3 from the SAME vocab.dropout_rng the resume branch minted and then never used -- a 19.7% relative error. This number is what SIG's one signature width (derive.signature_width_bytes) and DATA's splice-window gate are computed from on every resumed run, so a resume with dropout on trains with an undersized signature window and an optimistic splice gate, silently, on precisely the run type continual learning is measured across.
evidence: src/tok/api.py:244 mints `vocab.dropout_rng = _rng.rng_for("tok.dropout.mint", seed)` immediately before the replay, but :253 `ids, _pos = _segment(vocab, sample, dropout=0.0, stream=None)` never reads it -- the minted stream is dead on this branch. Compare :312 on the fresh-build path, `ids, _pos = _segment(vocab, sample, dropout=float(tok.dropout), stream=stream)`, which b95c4a4 introduced with the comment 'MEASURED WITH DROPOUT APPLIED, because the contract says "the COUNTING segmentation applies tok.dropout"... A dropout-free measurement describes a segmentation the TRAINING stream never produces.' Round 1's finding (p4_round1_findings.json, tok/api.py:296) named both sites as one defect ('same at line 243 on the replay path'); the repair's own commit message claims 'bytes_per_token is now measured WITH dropout applied, as the contract states... Identical at the 0.0 default' without qualifying that only one of the two sites changed.
fix: Change line 253 to `_segment(vocab, sample, dropout=float(tok.dropout), stream=vocab.dropout_rng)`, mirroring the fresh-build path's fix at line 312.

title: build_model's own frozen contract still names the stream "lm" as its seeding source and DID-IT-FIRE surface, but the repair moved the actual draw to a child stream "lm.init" without updating the docstring -- the documented verification surface can no longer distinguish build_model having run from it never being called.
failure: Any reader or tool that follows this entry point's own contract to check whether LM.build_model fired. The docstring at line 287-288 still reads 'Seeding: calls spine.rng.rng_for("lm", seed) and initialises every tensor from that one stream' and the DID IT FIRE line at 300 still names `rng.issued()["lm"]`, but the repaired body (line 310) draws from `rng_for("lm.init", int(seed))` instead -- "lm" is never touched by build_model any more. Since RUN.streams mints every name in compose.RNG_SUBSYSTEMS (which includes "lm") unconditionally at step 0 regardless of whether build_model is ever called, `rng.issued()["lm"]` is present in every process either way and carries no information about build_model having run. Verified: after RUN.streams(...) alone (no build_model call), `rng.issued()` already contains 'lm'; after also calling LM.build_model, `rng.issued()` gains 'lm.init' as a second, separately-seeded entry ((7250686939781505743, 0) for "lm" vs (4933293191311707615, 0) for "lm.init") while "lm"'s registration is byte-identical to the pre-build_model state. A reader who checks the documented surface exactly as written cannot tell 'build_model fired' from 'build_model was never called' -- the armed-vs-fired distinction this project's own DID IT FIRE convention exists to preserve collapses for this one entry point, and it collapses specifically because the repair fixed the code and not the contract describing it.
evidence: src/lm/api.py:287-288 ("Seeding: calls spine.rng.rng_for(\"lm\", seed)...") and :300 ("rng.issued()[\"lm\"]") are unchanged text from before the repair (git show b95c4a4 -- src/lm/api.py's diff hunk spans these exact lines and shows neither was edited). The body at :310 (`stream = _rng.rng_for("lm.init", int(seed))`) was changed by that same commit specifically to stop touching "lm" (see the comment immediately above it: 'A CHILD OF THE DECLARED PARENT, NOT A SECOND "lm"'). `grep -rn '"lm"' src/` confirms no code anywhere still calls `rng_for("lm", ...)`; the only surviving references to the bare name "lm" are these two stale docstring lines and the RNG_SUBSYSTEMS tuple in spine/compose.py that mints it at step 0 independent of build_model.
fix: Update line 287-288 to describe seeding via `rng_for("lm.init", seed)` (a child of the "lm" RUN.streams mints and never draws from), and change line 300's DID IT FIRE row to `rng.issued()["lm.init"]`, noting that "lm" itself is expected to report zero draws forever by design.
